name: FASTIMAGES
description: This dataset is the MEG portion of FASTIMAGES, a combined MEG and fMRI benchmark dataset for validating neural sequence replay detection methods in human neuroimaging data according to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS). Neural replay of past experiences has emerged as a widespread phenomenon hypothesized to be involved in many different cognitive processes, including decision making, memory consolidation, and planning. Yet, validating statistical methods used to detect replay is challenging due to the lack of a ground truth. FASTIMAGES addresses this by providing fast visual sequences of known structure that produce ground-truth neural activation sequences, paralleling the properties of replay. Thirty healthy participants (age: M = 24.2 years, SD = 2.9 years, range 20-35 years, 9 male, 21 female) were recorded with a MEGIN TRIUX MEG system (306 sensors) while viewing grayscale images of five categories (cat, chair, face, house, shoe) in a localizer condition and in fast sequence conditions with four onset-to-onset intervals (132, 164, 228, and 612 ms). The dataset enables benchmarking of sequence detection algorithms such as Temporally Delayed Linear Modelling (TDLM) and Slope Order Dynamic Analysis (SODA), and serves as an upper bound on method sensitivity under best-case conditions.
